hook: SCP-073 is a calm, courteous man who calls himself Cain, and the file leans hard on that name. Knowing the Genesis story of Cain and Abel helps the details land, though it is not required. It is a short, dense read where nearly every odd trait means something.
whyItMatters: Cain is one half of one of the site's best-known early pairings, with SCP-076 as the other, and readers tend to bring up the two numbers together. The beryllium bronze addendum also ties his artificial limbs to several other files, turning the article into a small hub for later worldbuilding. It shows how one character file can become a node other writers build around.
thingsToNotice:
Almost every anomaly is a piece of the biblical curse recast as a lab result: the ground fails where he walks, harm aimed at him comes back to whoever caused it, and he will not talk about the mark on his forehead. Read with that in mind, a property list becomes a portrait.

The decision to make him a living backup of Foundation records is a striking irony, trusting the first killer of legend as the most reliable archive. The last addendum is small but heavy: he politely declines to meet SCP-076, and the file leaves the reason unspoken.

related.note: The other half of the story, a far more violent figure Cain would rather avoid.
Named in the addendum as another object made with the same beryllium bronze.
